jurisdictions.name: Naperville
jurisdictions.portal_name: Permitting, Plans and Licensing Portal (Civic Access)
notes: Naperville requires a permit for every in-ground swimming pool and for most above-ground pools.
A pool, hot tub or spa must be surrounded by a barrier that meets the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code as adopted and amended by the city, and the rule applies to existing fences too.
Plans submitted on or after April 1, 2026 are reviewed against the 2024 IBC, 2024 IRC and 2024 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, with the 2023 National Electrical Code.
Projects with several features, such as a pool, patio and fence, need a permit for each feature; applicants file for the main feature and staff enter the others.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Permit - City of Naperville

jurisdictions.name: Joliet
jurisdictions.office: Building & Inspectional Services, Community Development (with Planning & Zoning review)
notes: Joliet's pool permit page requires a plat of survey marking the pool location, and building plans for in-ground pools.
Both a building permit and an electrical permit are required for in-ground and above-ground pools; the page cites NEC 2014 Article 680 for the electrical work.
Pools holding over 24 inches of water must be fenced at least 4 ft. high, and proof of a fence contract is required before the permit is issued.

The page gives minimum placement distances: 3 ft. from the property line, 6 ft. from the house, 5 ft. from underground power lines and 10 ft. from overhead lines, and no pools in front yards or required corner side yards.

sources.title: Residential Building Permit Information - City of Joliet

jurisdictions.name: Aurora
jurisdictions.office: Development Services Department, Division of Building and Permits
notes: Aurora's pool permit list directs applicants to its eTRAKiT online portal.
The city's pool application asks for manufacturer specifications for equipment and a proposed plat of survey with topographical and setback information.
The application lists the 2024 International Pool and Spa Code, 2024 IRC, 2024 IBC, 2023 National Electrical Code and 2014 State of Illinois Plumbing Code as applicable codes.
The owner's safety affidavit states the pool must be set outside all easements and 5 feet from property lines or fences, or 10 feet from alleys and exterior side lines on corner lots.

sources.title: Pools application (commercial or residential) - City of Aurora Division of Building and Permits

jurisdictions.name: Peoria
notes: Peoria's Building Safety page asks applicants to email permit applications to the Community Development Department.
The page says Peoria has adopted the 2018 International Building, Residential and related codes and the 2017 National Electrical Code, effective May 1, 2021.
The city's pool permit application says an electrical permit is required before or with the pool permit, and the applicant is responsible for barrier requirements.

sources.title: Application for Pool Permit - City of Peoria

gaps: Chicago: chicago.gov blocks automated access (403/Access Denied), so nothing was verified for Chicago.
Aurora: the eTRAKiT portal page itself was not opened; its listing page and the application that names it were.
Naperville: the Civic Access portal host was not opened; the city's Building Permits page that describes it was.
Peoria's pool application form is dated 1/26/09 on its face and the 2018 code adoption is from the 2021 notice; confirm current editions.
The Illinois state-level facts on the existing page (Public Act 103-0510, IDPH swimming facility code) were not re-verified here.
